_doc: Lakshly setup wizard sources catalog (setup-wizard.md §5). Public-safe: institution names, public sender domains and generic subject words only. Generated by specs/shared/gen_sources_catalog.py; edit that, not this file. Indian institutions first (region IN), then GLOBAL. Passwords are never stored: passwordHints are format descriptions only. 'verified' = date the sender domain was confirmed; null = check before shipping (CI prints the list).

queryRules.gmail: from:(<addresses + domains joined by OR>) [-from:<excludeDomain>…] subject:(<subjectAny joined by OR>) [has:attachment filename:pdf] newer_than:<window>
queryRules.outlook: (from:<a> OR from:<b>) [AND NOT from:<x>] AND (subject:<s1> OR subject:<s2>) [AND hasattachments:yes]
queryRules.quoting: subjectAny items are literal Gmail tokens; multi-word phrases are pre-quoted in the catalog.
queryRules.outlookUrl: Copy the AQS query to the clipboard, then open https://outlook.live.com/mail/0/ (outlook.com, hotmail.*, live.*, msn.com) or https://outlook.office.com/mail/ (work/school). Outlook on the web has no documented search URL.

passwordHintFormats.pan_caps: Your PAN in capital letters (10 characters: 5 letters, 4 digits, 1 letter).
passwordHintFormats.dob_ddmmyyyy: Your date of birth as DDMMYYYY.
passwordHintFormats.name4_dob_ddmm: First 4 letters of your name (the email says upper or lower case) followed by your birth day and month as DDMM.
passwordHintFormats.name4_card_last4: First 4 letters of the name on the card followed by the last 4 digits of the card.
passwordHintFormats.dob_ddmmyyyy_card_last4: Date of birth (DDMMYYYY) followed by the last 4 digits of the card, or the other way round, as the email says.
passwordHintFormats.mobile_last5_dob_ddmmyy: Last 5 digits of your registered mobile number followed by your date of birth as DDMMYY.
passwordHintFormats.customer_id: Your Customer ID, as shown in the bank's app or a recent alert.
passwordHintFormats.crn: Your CRN (customer relationship number), as shown in the bank's app or alert emails.
passwordHintFormats.cas_chosen: The password you chose when you requested the CAS.

gmail.exportOne: Open the email ▸ ⋮ (More) ▸ Download message. That saves a .eml file you can drop into Lakshly.
gmail.exportMany: Use the search, select all ▸ Label as 'Lakshly'. Then takeout.google.com ▸ Mail ▸ pick only the 'Lakshly' label ▸ export. You get an .mbox file.
gmail.attachment: Open the email ▸ hover the PDF ▸ Download. Lakshly asks for the PDF password on this device and never saves it.
gmail.filter: In the search bar ▸ Show search options ▸ Create filter ▸ Apply the label 'Lakshly' so new alerts collect in one place.

outlook.exportOne: Open the email ▸ … (More actions) ▸ Save / Download ▸ .eml.
outlook.exportMany: Move the found emails to a 'Lakshly' folder. On a Mac or PC, select them in the Outlook app and drag them to a folder on disk; each becomes a .eml file.
outlook.attachment: Open the email ▸ the PDF attachment ▸ Download.
outlook.filter: Settings ▸ Mail ▸ Rules ▸ Add new rule: From contains the sender ▸ Move to folder 'Lakshly'.

appleMail.exportOne: macOS Mail: drag the message to Finder (or File ▸ Save As ▸ Raw Message Source). iPhone Mail: open the PDF attachment ▸ Share ▸ Lakshly.

other.exportOne: Most mail apps can save a message as .eml or 'original'. Otherwise download the PDF attachment.
other.search: Search your mail for the sender domain and the subject words below.

guides.privacy: Lakshly never sees your inbox. These links only open your own mail in your browser or mail app. Files you import are read on this device.
